items.title: Fourteen Candidates Chase Open Ward 2 Seat as Tedjo Pursues Mississauga's Top Job
items.summary: TheLocal.to reports Ward 2 in Mississauga faces a wide-open council race after incumbent Alvin Tedjo chose to run for mayor instead of seeking re-election. According to the outlet, Tedjo was first elected to the seat in 2022 and later placed second to now-Mayor Carolyn Parrish in the 2024 mayoral byelection, giving him another shot at the top job this year. The outlet describes Ward 2 as one of the city's wealthiest, stretching along the Lake Ontario shoreline between the Credit River and Winston Churchill Boulevard, and including neighbourhoods such as Sheridan Homelands, Park Royal and the Lorne Park estates. TheLocal.to notes the ward is also home to the protected Rattray Marsh wetland, the province's busiest GO station in Clarkson, and the Southdown employment district, which includes the province's largest cement plant. With the seat now open, the outlet reports 14 candidates have registered, ranging from co-op housing activists to real estate investors.

items.title: Retired Police Detective Runs Sign-Free 'Community First' Bid for Mississauga Mayor
items.summary: The Pointer profiles Mike Matulewicz, a 75-year-old retired Toronto police detective running a grassroots campaign for Mississauga mayor without campaign signs, flyers or donation boxes. According to the outlet, Matulewicz says he will not canvass voters and will instead simply listen to residents about the issues affecting them, a philosophy he describes as community first. The Pointer reports he has pointed to rising car thefts and growing home-security concerns as symptoms of leadership that has failed local communities. The outlet says his platform calls for closing the $500-million shortfall Mississauga faces due to a gap in provincial funding, while improving emergency services, affordability, homelessness supports, public safety and housing. The Pointer notes his website cites the Metamorphosis network's Blueprint report, which found that Peel residents receive just 37 cents back in services for every tax dollar paid, compared with a 76-cent provincial average.

items.title: Rover and Redfin Rank Mississauga Fifth Among Canada's Best Cities for Dog Walks
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a new guide from pet-care company Rover and real estate firm Redfin ranked 11 Canadian cities for dog-walking, placing Mississauga fifth and Brampton tenth. According to the outlet, the companies also tracked which dog breeds are most popular and which are gaining ground fastest in each city. The outlet says the Cockapoo, a cross between a Cocker Spaniel and a Poodle, is the most popular breed in both Mississauga and Brampton. Insauga.com reports Boston Terriers are trending fastest in Mississauga, with a 78 per cent increase in pets added to Rover's data compared with the previous year, while Miniature Schnauzers lead the growth in Brampton at 232 per cent. The outlet says the figures are based on Rover's user-submitted data as of August 2026, with trending breeds determined by year-over-year growth among breeds that had at least 10 pets added during 2026.

items.title: Police Arrest Suspect After Midday Stabbing Near Hurontario and Dundas in Mississauga
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say a male suspect has been arrested in connection with a stabbing that happened near Hurontario Street and Dundas Street early Tuesday afternoon. According to police, the victim, described only as a male, was rushed to hospital with serious injuries and is now in stable condition. Insauga.com reports a large police presence remained on the scene after the attack as investigators and other officers spoke with people and canvassed the area. The outlet says motorists and others were urged to avoid the area while the stabbing was investigated as an isolated incident. Insauga.com notes the incident came nearly five months after a man was stabbed to death in an unrelated attack in the same area of the city.

items.title: OPP Charge Mississauga Man After Dark Web Drug Shipments Yield 600 Grams of Fentanyl
items.summary: According to the OPP, an investigation into drugs purchased on a dark web marketplace and shipped through the mail has led to charges against a Mississauga man. The OPP says the Caledon Community Street Crime Unit and the Covert Internet Intelligence Unit began investigating suspected drug shipments moving through the mail earlier in the summer. Officers say they arrested a suspect on Aug. 25 at a Canada Post location in Mississauga and seized two packages containing various drugs bound for addresses across Canada. The arrest led to raids of several residences and vehicles across the Greater Toronto Area, where the OPP says officers seized about 600 grams of suspected fentanyl, about 35 grams of suspected cocaine, $40,000 in cash, drug trafficking paraphernalia and numerous electronic devices. The OPP says Jermoll Bain, 33, of Mississauga, faces 16 counts of failing to comply with a release order, nine counts of possessing proceeds of crime over $5,000, and trafficking-related charges, while Jermaine Willis, 34, of North York, has been charged with possessing proceeds of crime over $5,000. Bain was due in a Brampton court Tuesday, and Willis is scheduled to appear Oct. 29, according to the OPP.

items.title: No Incumbent as Six Candidates Vie for Peel School Board Seat in Mississauga Wards 1 and 7
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports six candidates are competing for the Peel District School Board trustee seat covering Mississauga Wards 1 and 7 in the Oct. 26 election. According to the outlet, there is no incumbent in the race because sitting trustee Leeann Cole is instead running for the city's Ward 2 council seat. The outlet says Metroland sent a questionnaire to everyone on the ballot to help voters compare the candidates. Candidate Charles Corey told Metroland he serves as co-chair of his residents' association and volunteers with Safe City Mississauga as a team leader. Corey said he lives in Ward 6 but has grandchildren, family, friends and neighbours' kids attending schools across various Mississauga wards.

items.title: City Reverses Course on Aquitaine Avenue Bike Lanes to Restore Fourth Traffic Lane
items.summary: Insauga.com reports the City of Mississauga has removed bicycle lanes from a stretch of Aquitaine Avenue in Meadowvale as part of a plan to restore a fourth lane of vehicle traffic. According to the outlet, a city spokesperson confirmed the bike lanes, introduced in 2023 as part of a pilot project, have been eliminated, with a new in-boulevard multi-use path planned for cyclists and pedestrians instead. The outlet says the original Aquitaine Avenue Road Safety Pilot Project cut the busy four-lane road down to three lanes in summer 2023 to improve safety and reduce speeding, drawing mixed reviews from residents who objected to losing a traffic lane. Insauga.com reports the city decided to undo the pilot and restore the fourth lane following community feedback and new provincial legislation on bike lanes that took effect last December. The change is one of several road-safety initiatives the city has introduced in recent years, according to the outlet.
